old: An induction gathers scattered attention until quieter material becomes easier to hear. You don’t have to surrender, play asleep, or obey anyone. When you’re sober, distracted, analytical, or guarded, an actual induction may help. When meditation, loveyhuasca, lucid dreaming, grief, music, prayer, fatigue, or another intense opening has already made you trancey, begin with orientation and containment instead of adding depth.
new: The induction is a way to help you to pull your attention together so that you can hear material that might not reach you when you are soober. It is NOT a way to make you go asleep, surrender, or do anything you don’t want to do. If you are sober and having trouble focussing, too distracted, analytical, or are putting up a lot of resistance to working, an actual induction may help. However, if you are already pretty trancey from meditating beforehand, from loveyhuasca, lucid dreaming, working through grief, hearing music, praying, being tired, or for any other reason, you may want to skip to orienting and making sure you are contained.

old: Aim for the amount of trance that suits the practice: focused, warm, receptive, embodied, and still able to stop. Depth is optional.
new: If you do want to induce trance, choose as deep a trance as you need:

old: Tag questions—isn’t it, can’t it, doesn’t it—can soften a sentence. They become oily very quickly, don’t they? Use them lightly.
new: In the same way, tag questions (“isn’t it”, “can’t it”, “doesn’t it”, etc) can be very useful to soften a sentence. But they get oily really fast, so use them sparingly.

old: “The body already knows something about resting, doesn’t it?”
new: Doesn’t the body already know how to do this?

old: Nominalizations turn processes into nouns: healing, safety, trust, integration, communion, clarity, rest. Their vagueness can sometimes help because the subconscious supplies its own concrete meaning.
new: Nominalizations are words like healing, safety, trust, integration, communion, clarity, rest, and so on. Sometimes it’s good to use vague language, because then the subconscious fills in the blank with whatever is most appropriate and specific for that person.
